title: Open Source Agent Eval Harness Comparison 2026
tldr: The 2026 open-source agent eval harness landscape splits into five commercial platforms (LangSmith, Braintrust, Helicone, Phoenix, Promptfoo) and three OSS standards (OpenAI Evals, DeepEval v4, Inspect AI). DeepEval leads for pytest-style CI integration; Inspect AI dominates agent/capability eval at scale with async tool-use sandboxes; Ragas is the focused RAG-only pick. The eval market is consolidating — Promptfoo acquired by OpenAI ($86M), Braintrust raised $80M Series B. LangGraph is the production orchestration standard; CrewAI leads for rapid prototyping. Key benchmarks: SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, GAIA, WebArena, Tau-Bench. LLM-as-judge eval costs 30-50% of inference cost. Teams with best eval infra win — models are commodities, evaluation is differentiation.

open_source_eval_harnesses.name: DeepEval
open_source_eval_harnesses.strength: Pytest-native eval, G-Eval, DAG, agent, multi-turn, broad metric coverage, CI-friendly
open_source_eval_harnesses.best_for: CI-driven library-first evaluation with pytest integration

open_source_eval_harnesses.name: Inspect AI
open_source_eval_harnesses.strength: Async tool-use, sandboxes, agent and capability eval at scale, task-decorator style
open_source_eval_harnesses.best_for: Agent capability evaluation at scale with sandbox isolation

open_source_eval_harnesses.name: Ragas
open_source_eval_harnesses.strength: Reference-free RAG eval: faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, context recall

open_source_eval_harnesses.name: Promptfoo
open_source_eval_harnesses.strength: YAML-based prompt regression in CI, red-team plugins, acquired by OpenAI ($86M)
open_source_eval_harnesses.best_for: One-file CI gate for prompt regression testing

open_source_eval_harnesses.name: OpenAI Evals
open_source_eval_harnesses.strength: Reference implementation from OpenAI, broad benchmark coverage

open_source_eval_harnesses.name: MLflow Evaluate
open_source_eval_harnesses.strength: Bundled with MLflow platform, prompt + model comparison surface

open_source_eval_harnesses.name: Arize Phoenix
open_source_eval_harnesses.strength: OSS span viewer, OpenInference semantics, evaluation library

commercial_platforms.name: LangSmith

commercial_platforms.name: Braintrust
commercial_platforms.best_for: Enterprise eval with human feedback loops

agent_orchestration_frameworks.name: LangGraph
agent_orchestration_frameworks.strength: Durable state, checkpointing, time-travel debug, 87% task success rate (2026 benchmarks), production-proven at Klarna/LinkedIn/Uber

agent_orchestration_frameworks.name: CrewAI

agent_orchestration_frameworks.name: AutoGen

market_landscape.eval_cost: LLM-as-judge eval costs 30-50% of inference cost (e.g., $1,200-$2,000/month for $4K/month inference budget)
market_landscape.consolidation: Promptfoo acquired by OpenAI ($86M valuation); Braintrust $80M Series B at $800M valuation
market_landscape.key_trend_2026: Shift from single-agent to multi-agent orchestration; durable state across sessions; parallel orchestration; failure recovery; observability
market_landscape.production_adoption: 78% enterprise adoption of multi-agent systems, but <10% successfully scale
market_landscape.notable_quote: Teams shipping AI agents successfully in 2026 aren't the ones with the best models. They're the ones with the best evaluation infrastructure. Models are commodities. Evaluation is differentiation.

recommendations.for_production_evals: LangSmith (LangGraph teams) or Braintrust (enterprise with human feedback)
recommendations.for_production_orchestration: LangGraph (state machine, checkpointing, proven at scale)
